notes: Japan-market page (nintendo.co.jp), model TWL-001. status=partial ONLY because pixel resolution is missing (see below); dimensions, mass and both diagonals are primary-sourced. RESOLUTION NOT PUBLISHED: Nintendo states the panel size (3.25型) and type but no pixel count for the DSi on any page located — the JP DSi spec page, the JP DSi/DS Lite comparison table in the 2008-10-02 news release, the JP DSi LL three-way comparison page, Nintendo UK's 2008 'Nintendo introduces DSi' news page and Nintendo of America's archived DS systems comparison page all omit it. 256x192 appears only on non-acceptable sources (Wikipedia/spec aggregators), so resolution_px, aspect and active_area_mm are left null per THE RULE. Note Nintendo DOES publish 192×256 for the DS and DS Lite, but carrying that number across models is exactly the inference the spec forbids. Axis mapping: height=横137.0, width=縦74.9, depth=厚さ18.9; Nintendo's own label for the long axis is 'width' (横). Closed/folded state; open state not published. The 2008 news release lists these same figures under 本体サイズ（折りたたみ時）, which is the source for hinge.type=clamshell. controls[] left empty: neither the JP DSi spec page nor the comparison table enumerates the control set. ports: Nintendo lists a DS card slot, a full-size SD memory card slot, an AC adapter connector and a stereo headphone/mic connector — the SD slot is FULL-SIZE SD, NOT microSD, so it is omitted rather than recorded as the enum's 'microsd'; Nintendo does not state the headphone jack's 3.5 mm diameter. announced = date of Nintendo's own announcement release; released = Japan launch (the same release states 国外での「ニンテンドーＤＳｉ」発売は２００９年を予定, i.e. overseas in 2009, without a date). refresh_hz, materials, corner_radius, depth_at_hinge: not published, null. hinge.axis='long' from clamshell geometry, not a quoted line. || EVIDENCE SWEEP 2026-09-13: these values were present in the research pass but carried NO sources[] entry covering their field, so they were set to null per the registry rule (a value without a citation is an assertion, not evidence). Preserved verbatim here so a human can re-source rather than re-research: displays[0].panel = 'LCD'; displays[1].panel = 'LCD'.
